versions.text: Criterion: Verify that the fuel system functions safely under all specified conditions with the approved fuels and additives. Standard: Primary fuels allow continuous aircraft operation without any restrictions to aircraft envelope performance. Alternate/restricted fuels impose operational restrictions on the aircraft and may be used only when primary fuels are not available. Emergency fuels are used on a limited basis when an urgent need exists; their use imposes operational restriction and possible system damage. Fuels include required and allowed additives. Aircraft operating restrictions and additional maintenance actions are defined for each alternate/restricted and emergency fuel. Method of Compliance: Fuel system compatibility and performance with all specified air vehicle fuels, under all specified flight and environmental conditions, are verified using analyses, simulator tests, component tests, and ground/flight tests. References: JSSG-2009: E.3.4.5.1.1, E.4.4.5.1.1; E.3.4.5.1.2, E.4.4.5.1.2; E.3.4.5.1.3, E.4.4.5.1.3; E.3.4.5.1.4, E.4.4.5.1.4; E.3.4.5.2.1, E.4.4.5.2.1; E.3.4.5.2.2, E.4.4.5.2.2 14 CFR 23.951-23.979, 23.991-23.1001, 25.951-25.981, 25.991-25.1001, 27.951- 27.977, 27.991-27.999, 29.951-29.979, 29.992-29.1001 AC 20-29

Standard: The fuel system will function as required under all operating conditions and environments when using approved primary fuels. Alternate, restricted, and emergency fuels, and their limitations or restrictions are identified and documented. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Review of system requirements verify that primary, alternate, restricted, and emergency fuels and additives are identified.
(2) Review of flight and maintenance manuals verify limitations for the use of alternate, restricted, and emergency fuels and additives are provided to the flight and ground crew. Analysis.
  (1) Conduct analysis that shows air vehicle material compatibility with all required fuels and additives.
  (2) Conduct analysis of required fuel and additive types to determine what fuel and additive combinations need to be flight tested, and which combinations verify compatibility by similarity analysis to tested combinations. Test.
    (1) Lab test: Conduct lab tests to verify individual components and sub-assemblies of the fuel system meet performance requirements and are compatible with each fuel type and additive combination required for use in flight test.
    (2) Ground test: Conduct ground tests to verify the air vehicle meets performance requirements with each fuel type and additive combination required for use in flight test. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Test.
    (3) Flight test: Conduct flight test to verify the air vehicle meets performance requirements with each fuel type and additive combination determined as required for flight test by Analysis MoC (2).
